text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Project for new highway linking southern Croatian port of Ploce with Central Europe, which would pass through Bosnia, should be completed by end of the year. The World Bank, European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and other agencies are expected to provide financial assistance for this project, Bosnian minister for foreign trade and economy said.
- Another Moslem family from Croat-held western Mostar was expelled on Saturday, police in eastern Mostar say.

- Association of refugees from town of Brcko call on all pre-war residents of town to remain in area and for those displaced to prepare to return. Representative of Moslem-Croat federation says that Brcko refugees must respect whatever decision is taken by arbiter to settle Brcko dispute.
- Bosnian Moslems celebrated Bairam on Sunday, the most important Islamic holiday.
- A newspaper survey says a majority of 53 percent believe the federation is endangered by recent tensions.

- General Atif Dudakovic, Moslem commander of the Bosnian army 5th Corps, may be appointed deputy to General Rasim Delic, commander of the newly-created Moslem-Croat federation army. Such a promotion would displace a Croat general, Zivko Budimir.

- The air force of the federation army will be equipped only with helicopters for the moment and warplanes will be delivered at a later, unspecified date. An arms control agreement allows the federation 41 combat helicopters and 14 fighters.
- Agricultural Bank of Sarajevo will sign an agreement with Diner's Club branch office in Zagreb to offer Diner's club credit cards in Bosnia. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
